name: Creek Jump and Back-Up
note: Wyckoff's creek drawn properly: an OLS line through the three most recent interior swing highs (7-bar fractals) inside a contained range, required to slope down. The JUMP is one wide bar closing above that sloping line on heavy volume and near its high; the BACK-UP is a later narrow, low-volume bar that returns to the creek and holds above it; entry is the first close above the back-up bar's high. Any close half an ATR back below the creek aborts the setup and also exits the trade. Short is the mirror through swing lows on the ice line. Because the boundary slopes, this fires below where a horizontal Donchian break would, and it needs the expansion/contraction PAIR, not a single breakout bar. Note on scale: two thresholds are timeframe artefacts of the source's daily-bar quantification and are defaulted looser here with the literal values kept in the grid -- range containment (3.5*ATR(14) over 60 bars is unreachable intraday, where a 14-bar ATR spans a far shorter horizon than the 60-bar range) and back-up proximity (0.30*ATR from a creek that a >=1.3*ATR jump bar has just left behind). Everything else, including the 0.80 volume and spread contraction on the back-up bar and the 2-10 bar window, is exactly as specified.
source: Wyckoff's creek / jump-across-the-creek / back-up-to-the-edge-of-the-creek analogy, as taught in the StockCharts ChartSchool Wyckoff Method article and in Hank Pruden's codification of Wyckoff (The Three Skills of Top Trading, Wiley 2007). The OLS three-swing-point construction, slope constraint and all thresholds are the harvester's quantification (synthesis) -- the creek is drawn by hand in every source reachable.
